title: Yamada Denki says its reform management system was accessed without authorisation; customer data may have leaked
date_note: Security NEXT, dated 20 November, reports the company's disclosure; the company says it found the intrusion on 12 November. The disclosure day is not stated on the page, so the article's day is used.
summary: According to Security NEXT, Yamada Denki said a third party gained unauthorised access to its reform management system, found on 12 November. Customer names, addresses, phone numbers, renovation history and estimate data may have leaked, in up to 3.5 million records. The company says it has cut off external access and is still investigating the cause and scope.
plain: Yamada Denki says someone got into its renovation management system and customer details may have leaked, in up to 3.5 million records. It is still investigating.
exec: A possible leak of up to 3.5 million customer records at Yamada Denki raises impersonation and fraud risk for its customers.
action: If you are a Yamada Denki customer, be wary of calls, messages or emails claiming to be from the company, as the company itself warns.
impact: Up to 3.5 million records of customer data possibly leaked; number of people not stated.

validation.note: Security NEXT (Japan) report citing the company's disclosure. The company's own notice was not linked on the page and was not read.

review.note: Compared with Security NEXT (20 Nov): found 12 Nov, up to 3.5 million records, data types, access cut off, cause under investigation all match. Exec said 'major Japanese retailer', not on the page; now names the company only. Remains single_source.
